market_question: Will Charlie Kirk win the Nobel Peace Prize in 2026?
reasoning: Charlie Kirk is a conservative political activist with no history of peacemaking or humanitarian work; he is an implausible Nobel Peace Prize candidate. Even if he were named a joint laureate, the complex resolution rules give precedence to several better‑known figures (e.g., Trump, Zelenskyy), making his actual chances of being the market’s ‘single winner’ essentially zero. The market’s implied 1% probability is at least two orders of magnitude too high.
evidence_points: Charlie Kirk’s profile as a partisan activist makes him an extreme outlier among Nobel Peace Prize recipients, who are typically diplomats, humanitarians, or international organizations.
No credible forecasts or news sources list him as a candidate.

The resolution rules further reduce his chances: if any of Trump, Zelenskyy, Netanyahu, Putin, or Musk are joint laureates, the market resolves to the highest‑ranked of those, nullifying a Kirk win even in the single scenario where he might be awarded.
